description: Comprehensive Islamic terminology database for Swahili (Kiswahili) with Arabic loanwords, regional variations, and cultural context.

terms.definition_sw: Ibada ya nguzo ya pili ya Uislamu inayojumuisha visomo vya Qur'ani, rukuu, na sujudi kwa nyakati tano maalum za siku.
terms.definition_en: The second pillar of Islam, consisting of five obligatory daily prayers with specific recitations and physical postures.
terms.dialect_notes: In standard and coastal Swahili 'Swala' or 'Swalat' is common; 'Sala' is widely used across inland regions.

terms.definition_sw: Utakaso wa kiibada kwa kuosha viungo maalum vya mwili kabla ya kuswali au kushika Msahafu.
terms.definition_en: Ritual purification by washing specific body parts before performing prayer or touching the Quran.
terms.dialect_notes: Verb 'Kutawadha' (to perform wudu) is universal. In Kimvita/coastal dialect 'kuvua' or 'kuchukua udhu' is also heard.

terms.definition_sw: Kujizuia na kula, kunywa, na matamanio ya mwili kuanzia alfajiri ya kweli hadi machweo ya jua kwa nia ya ibada.
terms.definition_en: Fasting from dawn until sunset by abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations with religious intention.
terms.dialect_notes: Verb 'Kufunga' (to fast) is standard everywhere in East Africa.

terms.definition_sw: Kiwango maalum cha mali anachotoa Muislamu mwenye uwezo kwa wanaostahiki kila mwaka wa kiislamu.
terms.definition_en: Mandatory charitable contribution of a specified percentage of wealth given annually to eligible recipients.
terms.dialect_notes: Distinction made between 'Zaka ya Mali' (wealth zakat) and 'Zaka ya Fitri' (Ramadan end charity).

terms.definition_sw: Safari ya kiibada kuelekea Makkah kufanya matendo maalum katika mwezi wa Dhul-Hijjah mara moja maishani kwa mwenye uwezo.
terms.definition_en: The annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Makkah obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are physically and financially able.
terms.dialect_notes: Pilgrim who completed Hajj is honored with the title 'Al-Hajj' or 'Hajji' (male) / 'Hajjat' (female).

terms.definition_sw: Ziara ya kiibada Makkah inayojumuisha Ihramu, Tawafu ya Al-Kaaba, na Sayi baina ya Safa na Marwa wakati wowote wa mwaka.
terms.definition_en: The minor pilgrimage to Makkah that can be performed at any time of the year.
terms.dialect_notes: Often referred to as 'Hija ndogo' in colloquial East African Swahili.

terms.definition_sw: Utakaso mbadala wa Udhu au Ghusli kwa kutumia udongo safi iwapo maji hayapo au kuna udhuru wa kiafya.
terms.definition_en: Dry ritual purification using clean earth/dust when water is unavailable or cannot be used due to illness.
terms.dialect_notes: Standard across all regions.

terms.definition_sw: Kuosha mwili mzima kwa maji safi kwa nia ya kuondosha hadathi kubwa (janaba, hedhi, au nifasi).
terms.definition_en: Full ritual purification bath required to cleanse the major ritual impurity.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Kuoga janaba' is the common vernacular expression for ghusl.

terms.definition_sw: Wito rasmi wa kutangaza kuingia kwa wakati wa Swala unaonadiwa na Mwadhini kutoka msikitini.
terms.definition_en: The Islamic call to ritual prayer recited by the muezzin.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Mwadhini' is the person reciting adhan; 'Kumuadhini' is the action.

terms.definition_sw: Wito wa pili unaotolewa mara moja kabla ya kuanza kwa Swala ya jamaa kusimamisha safu.
terms.definition_en: The second call to prayer recited immediately before the congregational prayer commences.
terms.dialect_notes: Verb 'Kukimu' is used for reciting iqama.

terms.definition_sw: Mwelekeo wa Al-Kaaba tukufu mjini Makkah ambapo Waislamu wote huelekeza nyuso zao wanaposwali.
terms.definition_en: The direction that Muslims face during prayer, pointing towards the Kaaba in Makkah.
terms.dialect_notes: Common in all dialects; in East Africa, Qibla points north/north-east.

terms.definition_sw: Kitendo cha kuweka paji la uso, pua, viganja, magoti, na vidole vya miguu sakafuni kwa unyenyekevu mbele ya Allah.
terms.definition_en: The act of prostration in Islamic prayer where forehead, nose, hands, knees, and toes touch the ground.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Sajda ya Sahwi' (prostration of forgetfulness) and 'Sajda ya Tilawa' (recitation prostration) are frequently referenced.

terms.definition_sw: Kuinama kwa mgongo ulionyooka na kushika magoti huku ukimtukuza Mwenyezi Mungu katika Swala.
terms.definition_en: The bowing posture in Islamic prayer with hands on knees praising Allah.
terms.dialect_notes: Standard across Swahili literature.

terms.definition_sw: Swala za Sunnah za usiku zinazoswaliwa kwa jamaa baada ya Swala ya Isha katika mwezi wa Ramadhani.
terms.definition_en: Special voluntary night prayers performed in congregation during the month of Ramadan after Isha.
terms.dialect_notes: In East Africa commonly 8 or 20 rakaas followed by Witri.

terms.definition_sw: Swala ya Sunnah yenye fadhila kubwa inayoswaliwa katika theluthi ya mwisho ya usiku baada ya kuamka usingizini.
terms.definition_en: Voluntary late-night prayer performed after waking from sleep, highly recommended in Islam.
terms.dialect_notes: Often referred to as 'Swala ya Usiku'.

terms.definition_sw: Swala ya Sunnah yenye idadi ya rakaa tasa (isiyo ya namba shufwa, kama rakaa 1, 3, au 5) inayohitimisha swala za usiku.
terms.definition_en: An odd-numbered prayer that concludes the night prayers before dawn.
terms.dialect_notes: Standard across all madhhabs in East Africa.

terms.definition_sw: Kumtaja na kumkumbuka Mwenyezi Mungu kwa maneno matukufu kama Tasbih, Tahmid, Takbir, na Tahlil.
terms.definition_en: The remembrance and praise of Allah through repetitive recitation of divine names and glorification phrases.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Nyiradi' (plural of wirdi) is frequently used along the Swahili coast for daily dhikr routines.

terms.definition_sw: Maombi na unyenyekevu wa mja akimwomba Muumba wake haja za kidunia na za kiakhera.
terms.definition_en: Personal supplication and earnest prayer addressed directly to Allah asking for help, guidance, and forgiveness.
terms.dialect_notes: Universal across all Swahili speakers.

terms.definition_sw: Dini ya haki inayotokana na kujisalimisha kikamilifu kwa amri na mwongozo wa Mwenyezi Mungu na kufuata mafundisho ya Mtume Muhammad ﷺ.
terms.definition_en: The monotheistic religion of peace and submission to the will of Allah revealed through Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
terms.dialect_notes: Plural human noun: 'Waislamu'; singular: 'Mwislamu'; adjectival: 'Kiislamu'.

terms.definition_sw: Kushuhudia kwa ulimi na moyo ya kwamba hakuna mungu apasaye kuabudiwa kwa haki ila Allah na Muhammad ni Mtume Wake.
terms.definition_en: The Islamic declaration and testimony of faith asserting that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.
terms.dialect_notes: The foundational first pillar of Islam.

terms.definition_sw: Kumpwekesha Mwenyezi Mungu peke yake katika Uumbaji (Rububiyyah), Ibada (Uluhiyyah), na Majina na Sifa Zake (Asma wa Sifat).
terms.definition_en: The fundamental Islamic concept of the indivisible indivisible oneness and uniqueness of Allah.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Kumpwekesha Mwenyezi Mungu' is the standard Bantu explanation.

terms.definition_sw: Kumshirikisha Mwenyezi Mungu na kiumbe chochote katika uungu, mamlaka, au ibada; dhambi kubwa isiyosamehewa bila toba.
terms.definition_en: The sin of associating partners with Allah or polytheism; the gravest unforgivable sin without repentance.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Ushirikina' is also broadly used in Swahili culture for occultism/superstition, but in Aqidah means theological shirk.

terms.definition_sw: Kukiri kwa moyo, kutamka kwa ulimi, na kutenda kwa vitendo nguzo sita za imani katika Uislamu.
terms.definition_en: Faith in Islam, encompassing internal conviction, verbal affirmation, and righteous deeds.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Nguzo sita za Imani' (Six pillars of Faith) is taught in every madrasa across East Africa.

terms.definition_sw: Viumbe wa nuru walioumbwa na Mwenyezi Mungu wasiotenda dhambi na wanaotii amri Zake zote (kama Jibril, Mikail, Israfil, n.k.).
terms.definition_en: Celestial beings of light created by Allah who never sin and execute divine commands.
terms.dialect_notes: Plural and singular form in Swahili is typically 'Malaika'.

terms.definition_sw: Wajumbe wateule wa kibinadamu waliotumwa na Allah kuwaongoza wanadamu, akiwemo Nabii Muhammad ﷺ akiwa mtume wa mwisho.
terms.definition_en: Chosen human messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity, culminating in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as the final messenger.
terms.dialect_notes: Singular: 'Mtume' (Messenger / Rasul) and 'Nabii' (Prophet / Nabi).

terms.definition_sw: Maisha ya milele yanayoanza baada ya kifo na Siku ya Kiyama ambapo watu watalipwa Pepo au Moto kulingana na matendo yao.
terms.definition_en: The eternal afterlife following the Day of Judgment where individuals are rewarded with Paradise or punished in Hellfire.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Siku ya Mwisho' is the indigenous Bantu phrase for the Day of Judgment.

terms.definition_sw: Makazi ya milele ya neema na furaha aliyowaandalia Mwenyezi Mungu waja Wake wema na waumini katika Akhera.
terms.definition_en: The eternal paradise and abode of bliss prepared by Allah for the righteous believers in the Hereafter.
terms.dialect_notes: Both 'Pepo' (Bantu origin) and 'Jannah' (Arabic loanword) are universally understood.

terms.definition_sw: Makazi ya adhabu na mateso ya moto kwa makafiri na waasi katika maisha ya Akhera.
terms.definition_en: The realm of punishment and hellfire for disbelievers and unrepentant transgressors in the Hereafter.
terms.dialect_notes: Also colloquially 'Moto wa Akhera'.

terms.definition_sw: Mpango na makadirio ya milele ya Mwenyezi Mungu juu ya kila kinachotokea ulimwenguni, kheri na shari.
terms.definition_en: The divine preordainment and absolute destiny decreed by Allah over all creation.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Majaliwa' is the widely used East African Swahili word for divine destiny.

terms.definition_sw: Kila kitu au kitendo ambacho Sharia ya Kiislamu imekiruhusu bila makatazo wala dhambi.
terms.definition_en: Everything that is legally permissible and lawful according to Islamic law.
terms.dialect_notes: In standard Swahili ends with vowel 'i' (Halali).

terms.definition_sw: Kila tendo au kitu kilichokatazwa wazi na Sharia ya Kiislamu ambacho mkosaji anastahili adhabu na anayekiacha anapata thawabu.
terms.definition_en: Strictly prohibited by Islamic jurisprudence; committing it incurs sin and punishment while avoiding it earns reward.
terms.dialect_notes: In standard Swahili ends with vowel 'u' (Haramu).

terms.definition_sw: Wajibu wa lazima uliothibiti kwa dalili ya mkato; mwenye kutenda anapata thawabu na mwenye kuacha kwa makusudi anapata dhambi.
terms.definition_en: An absolute mandatory obligation in Islamic law; performing it is rewarded and omitting it is sinful.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Fardhi ya Ain' (individual duty) and 'Fardhi ya Kifaya' (communal duty) are key concepts.

terms.definition_sw: Matendo aliyoyafanya au kuyahimiza Mtume Muhammad ﷺ; mtendaji anapata thawabu lakini anayeacha hapati dhambi.
terms.definition_en: Recommended religious practices following the tradition of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ; rewarding if done but not sinful if omitted.
terms.dialect_notes: Universal across East Africa.

terms.definition_sw: Kitendo kilichochukiwa katika Sharia lakini hakikufikia kiwango cha haramu; anayeacha anapata thawabu na anayetenda haadhibiwi.
terms.definition_en: Discouraged or disliked actions; leaving them is rewarded, but performing them is not strictly sinful.
terms.dialect_notes: Standard across all legal texts in Swahili.

terms.english_equivalent: Neutral / Permissible with no specific reward or penalty
terms.definition_sw: Kitendo kilicho sawa kiholela ambacho hakina amri ya kufanya wala katazo, hakina thawabu wala dhambi chenyewe.
terms.definition_en: Neutral actions in Islamic jurisprudence with no specific religious praise or blame.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Ruhusa' or 'Mubaha' is used.

terms.definition_sw: Shule au mfumo wa kifiqhi unaofuata mbinu za mmoja wa maimamu wakuu (Shafi'i, Hanafi, Maliki, Hanbali).
terms.definition_en: A classical school of Islamic jurisprudence following the methodology of one of the major imams.
terms.dialect_notes: Madhehebu ya Shafi'i is the historical majority school throughout the Swahili coast and East Africa.

terms.definition_sw: Hakimu wa Kiislamu mwenye mamlaka kisheria kutoa hukumu katika Mahakama ya Kadhi kuhusu ndoa, talaka, na mirathi.
terms.definition_en: An Islamic judge presiding over a Kadhi court handling Muslim personal law such as marriage, divorce, and inheritance.
terms.dialect_notes: Established constitutional institution in Kenya and Zanzibar ('Mahakama za Kadhi' / 'Chief Kadhi').

terms.definition_sw: Ufafanuzi au hukumu ya kisheria inayotolewa na Mufti au mwanazuoni anayetambuliwa kujibu swali la kidini.
terms.definition_en: A non-binding formal legal opinion provided by a qualified Islamic scholar or Mufti.
terms.dialect_notes: Issued by Mufti of Tanzania (BAKWATA), Zanzibar Mufti Office, or Supreme Council of Scholars.

terms.definition_sw: Faida ya nyongeza isiyo ya haki inayotozwa au kulipwa kwenye mikopo au ubadilishanaji mali, iliyoharamishwa kabisa katika Uislamu.
terms.definition_en: Unjustified excess, usury, or interest charged on loans, strictly forbidden in Islamic law.
terms.dialect_notes: Universal term.

terms.definition_sw: Misaada na hisani ya hiari anayoitoa Muislamu kwa ajili ya kutafuta radhi za Mwenyezi Mungu.
terms.definition_en: Voluntary charity and benevolence given for the pleasure of Allah.
terms.dialect_notes: In Swahili, 'Sadaka' also encompasses everyday benevolent acts.

terms.definition_sw: Kuzuia mali (kama ardhi, jengo, au msikiti) isinunuliwe wala kuuzwa bali manufaa yake yatumike kwa hisani na maslahi ya jamii ya Kiislamu.
terms.definition_en: An inalienable charitable endowment in Islamic law typically dedicating property for religious and philanthropic purposes.
terms.dialect_notes: Zanzibar and Kenyan Coast have historical Wakf / Waqf Commissions governing endowed properties.

terms.definition_sw: Mkataba mtakatifu wa kisheria unaofungwa baina ya mume na mke kwa idhini ya walii, mashahidi, na mahari halali.
terms.definition_en: The sacred Islamic marriage contract contracted between groom and bride with guardian consent, witnesses, and mahr.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Kufunga pingu za maisha' or 'kufunga ndoa ya Kiislamu'.

terms.definition_sw: Mali au zawadi ya lazima anayopewa bi harusi na bwana harusi wakati wa kufunga ndoa kuwa miliki yake binafsi.
terms.definition_en: The mandatory dower or gift given by the groom directly to the bride as her sole property upon marriage.
terms.dialect_notes: In Kimvita/coastal dialects sometimes 'Mahare'. It belongs solely to the bride, not her parents.

terms.definition_sw: Kuvunja mkataba wa ndoa kisheria kwa matamshi maalum chini ya taratibu za Kiislamu.
terms.definition_en: The Islamic dissolution of marriage under prescribed legal procedures.
terms.dialect_notes: Handled through Kadhi courts or family arbitration.

terms.english_equivalent: Waiting Period after Divorce or Bereavement
terms.definition_sw: Kipindi maalum cha kungojea ambacho mwanamke aliyefiwa na mumewe au kupewa talaka lazima akae kabla ya kuolewa tena.
terms.definition_en: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of her husband before remarrying.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Kukaa Eda' is the universal Swahili term.

terms.definition_sw: Mgawanyo wa kisheria wa mali ya marehemu kwa warithi wake kulingana na hisa zilizoainishwa ndani ya Qur'ani Tukufu.
terms.definition_en: The distribution of the deceased's estate among lawful heirs according to Quranic proportions.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Urithi' is general inheritance; 'Mirathi' is specific to Islamic Sharia estate distribution.

terms.definition_sw: Neno la Mwenyezi Mungu lililoteremshwa kwa Mtume Muhammad ﷺ kupitia Malaika Jibril, likiwa muujiza na mwongozo wa maisha.
terms.definition_en: The verbatim word of Allah revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through Angel Gabriel, the primary sacred scripture of Islam.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Msahafu' refers to the physical bound volume.

terms.definition_sw: Maneno, vitendo, maamuzi, au sifa za Mtume Muhammad ﷺ zilizopokewa kupitia mlolongo wa wasimulizi wa kuaminika.
terms.definition_en: Recorded sayings, actions, approvals, and characteristics of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with chains of narration.
terms.dialect_notes: Plural and singular in Swahili is 'Hadithi'.

terms.definition_sw: Ufafanuzi na ufafanuzi wa kina wa maana, miktadha ya kuteremka, na hekima za aya za Qur'ani Tukufu.
terms.definition_en: Scholarly exegesis, commentary, and contextual explanation of the verses of the Quran.
terms.dialect_notes: Famous Swahili translations/tafsirs include those by Sheikh Abdullah Saleh Al-Farsy and Sheikh Ali Muhsin Al-Barwani.

terms.definition_sw: Kumuogopa Mwenyezi Mungu, kutekeleza maamrisho Yake yote, na kujiepusha na makatazo Yake kwa unyenyekevu.
terms.definition_en: Piety, god-consciousness, and reverential fear of Allah leading to adherence to divine commandments.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Uchaji Mungu' is the quintessential Swahili translation of Taqwa.

terms.definition_sw: Kumuabudu Mwenyezi Mungu kana kwamba unamuona, na ikiwa humuoni basi tambua ya kwamba Yeye anakuona.
terms.definition_en: The highest spiritual state of worshipping Allah as though you see Him, knowing that He sees you.
terms.dialect_notes: Standard across all religious texts.

terms.definition_sw: Kujuta kwa dhati kutokana na dhambi, kuiacha mara moja, na kuweka azma thabiti ya kutoirudia tena kwa ajili ya Allah.
terms.definition_en: Sincere repentance to Allah for sins committed, accompanied by regret and determination not to return to them.
terms.dialect_notes: Verb is 'Kutubu' (to repent).

terms.definition_sw: Kudumu katika utiifu kwa Allah, kujizuia na maasi, na kuvumilia mitihani na mikasa ya kidunia bila malalamiko.
terms.definition_en: Patience, steadfastness, and endurance in obeying Allah and facing life's tribulations.
terms.dialect_notes: Swahili proverb: 'Subira huvuta heri' (Patience brings blessing).

terms.definition_sw: Kutambua na kushukuru neema za Mwenyezi Mungu kwa moyo, ulimi (Alhamdulillah), na matendo mema.
terms.definition_en: Expressing gratitude and praise to Allah for His boundless bounties.
terms.dialect_notes: Universal daily expression across East Africa.

terms.arabic_original: المجلس الأعلى للشؤون الإسلامية في تنزانيا
terms.definition_sw: Baraza Kuu la Waislamu Tanzania linalosimamia masuala ya kijamii, kielimu, na kidini ya Waislamu wa Tanzania Bara chini ya Mufti Mkuu.
terms.definition_en: The apex national Islamic organization overseeing Muslim religious and social affairs in mainland Tanzania.
terms.dialect_notes: Tanzania specific; led by the Mufti Mkuu wa Tanzania.

terms.definition_sw: Kiongozi mkuu wa mahakama za Kadhi nchini Kenya na Zanzibar anayesimamia utatuzi wa kisheria wa masuala ya ndoa, talaka, na mirathi ya Kiislamu.
terms.definition_en: The judicial head of the Kadhi court system in Kenya and Zanzibar overseeing Islamic personal law.
terms.dialect_notes: Key legal figure in Kenyan coastal and national Islamic affairs and Zanzibar.

terms.definition_sw: Kusoma visa na mashairi ya sifa na historia ya Mtume Muhammad ﷺ katika mwezi wa Rabi' al-Awwal na mikusanyiko ya kidini.
terms.definition_en: The commemoration of the birth and life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ celebrated through poetry, Quran recitation, and religious gatherings.
terms.dialect_notes: Lamu Maulid (Riyadha Mosque) and Zanzibar Maulid festivals are celebrated cultural landmarks of Swahili Islamic heritage.

terms.definition_sw: Chakula kinacholiwa wakati wa machweo ya jua kwa ajili ya kufungua saumu wakati wa mwezi wa Ramadhani au saumu za sunnah.
terms.definition_en: The evening meal with which Muslims end their daily Ramadan fast at sunset.
terms.dialect_notes: 'Kufuturu' is the verb; 'Futari' is the meal. Traditional East African items include mahamri, vitumbua, tende, uji wa ngano.

terms.definition_sw: Chakula cha mapema kinacholiwa kabla ya kuingia kwa alfajiri ili kupata nguvu ya kufunga saumu ya siku hiyo.
terms.definition_en: The pre-dawn meal consumed by Muslims before starting the daily fast.
terms.dialect_notes: Indigenous Bantu term 'Daku' is universally used across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, and Comoros.

terms.definition_sw: Nyumba takatifu ya ibada ya Waislamu ambamo huswaliwa Swala tano, Swala ya Ijumaa, na hufanyika mafunzo ya kidini.
terms.definition_en: The Muslim place of worship where congregational prayers and religious instruction take place.
terms.dialect_notes: Plural: 'Misikiti'. Historical coral mosques (e.g. Kilwa Great Mosque, Kizimkazi) date back over 1000 years.

terms.definition_sw: Kituo au shule ya elimu ya Kiislamu ambapo watoto na watu wazima hujifunza kusoma Qur'ani, Fiqhi, Tawhidi, na lugha ya Kiarabu.
terms.definition_en: An Islamic educational institution where students learn Quran recitation, Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and Arabic.
terms.dialect_notes: In coastal dialects (Kimvita/Kiamu/Kiunguja), 'Chuo' historically referred specifically to the children's Quran school.

terms.definition_sw: Mwalimu anayefundisha masomo ya dini ya Kiislamu, Qur'ani, na Kiarabu katika madrasa au msikiti.
terms.definition_en: A respected instructor or teacher of Islamic studies and Quranic sciences.
terms.dialect_notes: Plural: 'Maustadhi'. Female form: 'Ustaadhat'.

terms.definition_sw: Mwanazuoni au kiongozi mwenye elimu pana ya Sharia na mafundisho ya Kiislamu anayeheshimika katika jamii.
terms.definition_en: A distinguished Islamic scholar or community elder with deep religious knowledge.
terms.dialect_notes: In standard Swahili both 'Sheikh' (pl. 'Masheikh') and 'Shehe' (pl. 'Mashehe') are widespread.

terms.definition_sw: Sikukuu mbili kuu za Kiislamu: Iddi ndogo (Eid al-Fitr mwishoni mwa Ramadhani) na Iddi kubwa (Eid al-Adha / Sikukuu ya Kuchinja).
terms.definition_en: The two major Islamic festive holidays: Eid al-Fitr marking the end of Ramadan, and Eid al-Adha celebrating the sacrifice.
terms.dialect_notes: In East Africa 'Iddi ndogo' = Eid al-Fitr; 'Iddi kubwa' or 'Sikukuu ya Kuchinja' = Eid al-Adha.
